extracted.intended_audience: Navy managers and policymakers implementing OMB Circular A-76; contract administrators; researchers studying federal contracting-out/post-award performance
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of post-award costs, performance, and implementation issues arising from contracting out under OMB Circular A-76, focusing on Navy supply operations (food service and storage/warehousing). Includes measurement of cost savings, performance metrics, administrative burdens, and policy guidance needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for post-award guidance and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The study identifies 'the need for post-award guidance and policy' as a major issue in CA program implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thesis recommends development of centralized post-award guidance and policy to address problems that emerge after contract award (e.g., monitoring, dispute resolution, contract modifications, performance shortfalls).

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for centralized claimant guidance at the field level
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit identification of 'the need for increased claimant guidance at the field level.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide claimant (units receiving services) guidance and direction so claimants understand requirements, expectations, and how to interact with contractors and contract administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of cost accounting system and post-award program controls
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'absence of an adequate cost accounting system and post-award program controls' is cited as a key issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A robust cost accounting system is required to capture relevant costs and to track actual post-award expenditures and savings; without it, comparisons and program assessments are unreliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient contract administration staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: The study notes 'the need for increased contract administration staffing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure adequate staffing (titles, grades, full/part-time allocation) dedicated to contract administration to handle oversight, documentation, inspections, deductions, and dispute response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of budget flexibility after contracting out
rubrics_metrics.description: Identified problem: 'a problem with budget flexibility at activities that have contracted out.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and mitigate how contracting out affects local budget flexibility, ability to reallocate funds, and resource management at the activity level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and accuracy of performance definition (PWS/PRS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuing problems with 'performance definition' and the use of Performance Requirements Summary (PRS) for deductions and measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance statements must be well-defined, not easily gamed; ensure PRS proxies accurately reflect true service quality and avoid narrow metrics that encourage manipulation (apple color analogy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of pre-award cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Central controversy: assumption that 'a pre-award bid to perform a particular function is an accurate estimate of the actual post-award cost.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and validate pre-award bidding assumptions against post-award experience; identify common underestimates and adjust methodology or include contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant costs and incremental cost principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: relevant costs are 'expected future costs (expected future revenues) that will differ among alternatives' and incremental cost is 'the difference in total cost between two alternatives.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost comparisons should include only relevant future costs that differ between in-house and contract alternatives; exclude sunk and costs that would be incurred regardless of choice; compute incremental costs for decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution using proxies/surrogate measures for performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Because performance cannot be measured directly, 'proxies' or surrogate measures are used, but they may not accurately reflect quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select performance proxies carefully, monitor for measurement manipulation, and supplement quantitative proxies with qualitative assessments where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-phase CA program implementation process
rubrics_metrics.description: The CA implementation process consists of four phases: inventory, management review, cost comparison, and implementation of the results of the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each phase is conducted thoroughly: inventory to identify reviewable functions; management review for special circumstances; rigorous cost comparison; and controlled implementation/transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of cost comparison methodology: incremental vs full cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Debate over whether in-house costs should be determined on an incremental or fully allocated basis; 1983 moved methodology to simpler incremental approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about whether an incremental or full-cost approach is used; understand how methodological choice affects comparison outcomes and controversy (some elements were replaced by standard cost factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized cost factors and Cost Comparison Handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cost Comparison Handbook provides standard cost factors and instructions intended to provide a uniform methodology for making cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow handbook procedures and standard factors to improve comparability and reduce contested complex computations; but remain vigilant for factors that may misstate real costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: MEO (Most Efficient Organization) savings calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: MEO savings: computed based on the number of positions eliminated by implementation of the MEO; savings calculated for 3 years using cost per position from NAVCOMPT Budget Exhibit OP-03.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When computing in-house (MEO) savings, use consistent period (typically 3 years) and authoritative per-position cost figures; document assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion savings calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion savings: difference between in-house and contract bids, calculated for the period covered by the cost comparison (usually 3 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate conversion savings over the full comparison period; ensure contract bids and in-house estimates are comparable in scope and inclusive of relevant costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program expense (CA administrative positions) and payback
rubrics_metrics.description: Program expense equals salary costs of dedicated CA administrative positions; used to compute program net savings and payback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include program administrative costs when reporting net savings and payback; track number of positions and per-position cost annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage and warehousing performance metrics (Appendix B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics to collect before and after award: receipt-to-stow on-time (%), issues on-time (%), warehouse refusals (%), shipped on-time (%), receipt accuracy (%), issue accuracy (%), ability to meet emergency requirements, general warehouse appearance (cleanliness), local deliveries on-time, # safety violations, # incoming Reports of Discrepancy (RODs), % items properly packed for shipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect these objective metrics pre- and post-award to compare operational performance; use consistent definitions and record-keeping to ensure comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food service performance metrics (Appendix B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics to collect before and after award: sanitation inspection results, equipment maintenance, financial returns (over or under issue), cycle menu development, customer satisfaction indicators, attendance levels, # safety violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track sanitation, maintenance, financial, menu, and satisfaction metrics pre/post-award; quantify and document changes attributable to contracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria used to judge contractor performance (survey list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common criteria: Observation, Routine Command Performance indicators, Timeliness measures, Accuracy measures, Safety measures, Customer satisfaction measures, External inspection results, Internal audit results, Quality Assurance inspection results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a mix of observational, administrative, audit, and customer-focused measures to assess contractor performance; document which criteria were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deductions for substandard performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether deductions for substandard performance were taken; document how many deductions, average monthly amount, cumulative amount, and which performance areas were deficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain logs of deductions, reasons, and amounts to evaluate enforcement of PRS and financial impact of performance shortfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other actions related to contractor performance (CDRs, claims, litigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track actions such as Contract Deficiency Reports, claims, litigation proceedings; record dollar amounts involved, results, and documentation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document frequency, cost, and administrative burden of disputes and claims as part of post-award cost accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award survey and technical proposal evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine if a pre-award survey was conducted (who performed it and what was done); whether a technical proposal was required and who evaluated proposals and how long it took.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record pre-award due diligence and technical evaluation processes as factors affecting post-award performance and transition success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency and nature of PWS modifications during contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess if contracts experienced many modifications to the Performance Work Statement (PWS); changes may include scope of work, procedural changes, deduction schedule, PRS; note effect on contract price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track PWS modifications and their reasons and cost impacts; frequent changes may indicate inadequate original performance definition or changing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of contractor experience
rubrics_metrics.description: How contractor experience is assessed: references, previous work with Navy, on-site visits of other operations, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify contractor capability through documented references, prior performance, and site visits to reduce post-award performance risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative costs and unanticipated admin burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify additional administrative costs associated with administering the contract not anticipated (e.g., clocking devices, dealing with disputes, excessive documentation requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include extra admin costs in post-award cost accounting and when judging whether contracting out realized net savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damage to government facilities and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether the contractor caused damage beyond normal wear and tear, dollar amount of damages, and whether similar damages occurred under government operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track facility/equipment damage claims and repair costs as part of post-award cost and risk assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract award type and procurement method
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether the award was sealed bid, negotiated procurement, or neither, and whether changes in award type affect post-award outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider procurement method as a factor in contractor selection quality, price stability, and potential for disputes/changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevalence and impact of contract price changes during performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Track whether the original bid dollar amount changed during the course of the contract and reasons (mandatory pay raises, change in scope/mission, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and document mid-contract price changes to assess bid accuracy and contract management efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition costs and litigation costs frequently not accounted for
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey options include flags that cost comparisons may omit: 'Transition costs are more than 10% differential', 'Litigation costs are not accounted for', etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly include transition costs, litigation/claims costs, and other one-time conversion costs in cost-comparison analyses to avoid overstating savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs for administering RIF procedures and impact on remaining government workers' productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparison omissions may include costs of administering Reduction-in-Force (RIF) procedures and productivity impacts on remaining government workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for personnel reduction-related administrative costs and indirect effects (morale/productivity) when evaluating contracting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy and credibility of in-house cost data
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO finding: 'Complete and accurate in-house cost data is not readily available.' Lack of reliable in-house cost data undermines cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure in-house cost data collection systems are complete, standardized, and auditable prior to conducting cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability and accuracy of the government retirement cost factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncertainty and controversy over the appropriate retirement cost factor (e.g., historical fluctuations from 7% to 27.05%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about retirement factor assumptions and update them to reflect policy changes; sensitivity-test comparisons to retirement factor variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification and objectivity of personnel preparing cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO observed cost comparisons 'lack credibility in some cases because they are often prepared by personnel who are unqualified or would be affected by actions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign qualified, neutral staff to prepare cost comparisons or use independent reviewers to improve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of required reviews and schedule adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO noted 'required reviews of the commercial or industrial activities are far behind schedule.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain schedules for inventories, reviews, and re-studies as required (e.g., Executive Order timelines) to ensure continuing cost-effectiveness assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and vulnerability of Performance Requirements Summary (PRS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRS 'can easily become the focus for measurement manipulation' and may not capture true quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design PRS with safeguards against manipulation, validate PRS outcomes with independent checks, and include broader quality indicators.
